subject: Conrad corpse use protocol and shortest evidenced post-soldier approach
scope: Static disassembly of byte-identical original 1.16.5.0 client modules, original usable table, and retained copied-client checkpoints; no client/harness run or gameplay/live change

client_protocol.exact_source: trpython.zip:client/augmentations/usable.pyo Usable.OnGetUseAction line 305 offsets 0-15 and OnUse line 420 offsets 0-42; client/augmentations/actor.pyo Actor.PerformUseObject line 1855 offsets 0-132; client/inputhandlers.pyo Use lines 238-265 as audited in docs/evidence/bootcamp-s5-soldier-client-use-protocol-20260924.md
client_protocol.finding: A usable's action invokes OnUse, which resolves the player and calls PerformUseObject for the selected entity. The actor creates a UseObject action, fills windupTimeMs from the usable, and performs it. In FPS mode the use input is the right-button press; in MMO mode it is release without a use drag. An actual object target and visible 'Press [Mouse Button 2] to use' prompt are more probative than proximity to a quest marker.
client_protocol.limit: Input mode and aim must be observed in the particular run; the original client path does not establish the final-live corpse class or windup.

client_protocol.exact_source: trpython.zip:client/actions/useobject.pyo UseObject class line 22 offset 12; CheckAction line 66 offsets 0-244; _InUseRadiusOf line 108 offsets 0-174; SendServerRequest line 129 offsets 0-47
client_protocol.finding: UseObject has checkRange=1. CheckAction rejects dead actor, missing/wrong usable, mismatched action argument, locked unusable, out-of-range target, and failed _world.InLineOfSight(actor.body,usable.body). Only after those checks does SendServerRequest call SendCallActorMethod('RequestUseObject', (actionId,actionArgId,usable.entityId)+useArgs). The range check uses 3D squared distance from actor.body.GetPosition() to usable.body.GetHPSWorldPosition(DAMAGE1), and compares it to max(actor.GetUseRange(),usable.GetUsableMaxRange()) squared.
client_protocol.limit: Native InLineOfSight and DAMAGE1 geometry are not reconstructed by this Python bytecode. A missing RequestUseObject can result from acquisition, range, line of sight, state or input; it does not prove a server rejection.

client_protocol.exact_source: trpython.zip:client/augmentations/actor.pyo Actor.__init__ line 256 bytecode offsets 308-314 initializes __useRange=3; generated/client/usabledata.pyo usableMaxRange assignment offsets 85167-85179 contains only class 26232=16; trpython.zip:client/augmentations/usable.pyo _GetUsableMaxRange line 123 and GetUsableMaxRange line 276
client_protocol.finding: The base actor use range is 3 m. The original table has no override for current analogue class 21961, so GetUsableMaxRange returns its default zero and the nominal client action range for this class is 3 m, measured to the model's DAMAGE1 connection point. The actor's use range is mutable, and no runtime range modifier was measured in the copied character.
client_protocol.limit: Class 21961 is an analogue; the lost final-live Conrad entity may have had another class, max range, model connection point or server-side rule.

shortest_evidenced_movement.source: docs/evidence/bootcamp-s5-corpse-approach-20260924.json setup and run 67; docs/evidence/bootcamp-s5-corpse-use-20260924.json run 04 step4-west.png and run 09 step1-hover.png, step2-after-rightclick.png, game.log line 123
shortest_evidenced_movement.ordinary_movement_from_login: S 1000 ms, A 1650 ms, W 850 ms in run 04; endpoint (-94.73047,84.99609,65.640625). Run 03 used S 1000 ms, A 1000+650 ms, W 850 ms and reached (-94.695,85.031,66.063) with the same prompt. These are the shortest recorded successful ordinary movement sequences from the copied post-dialogue checkpoint, not guaranteed repeatable directions or durations.
shortest_evidenced_movement.viewpoint_limit: The prompt at a center distance over 3 m is consistent with the client's DAMAGE1 connection-point calculation; it cannot identify the point's actual offset. The object is inferred class 21961 at (-98.0,85.39,67.2), with ±30 m final-live horizontal uncertainty. The run 04 endpoint was ordinary-reached, but the successful use was a separate run 09 after a copied login-coordinate edit to that reached point.
shortest_evidenced_movement.navmesh_comparison: Read-only query from prior dialogue coordinate (-102.39844,86.68221,73.4375) to use viewpoint reports a complete 12.3 m path via (-96.0,86.1,70.8), (-95.6,85.9,69.2), (-94.7,85.4,65.6). The ordinary run supports an east-side bypass, while navmesh corners alone are not an exact client movement trace.

observed_use_transition: At the copied run-09 viewpoint the client showed 'Salvagable Materials' and 'Press [Mouse Button 2] to use'. A short right-click at screen pixel (740,386) sent RequestUseObject; the client showed objective 3 completed, switched to 'Destroy the crashed dropship before the bomb timer expires' with 00:09:59, and the copied database persisted objective 3 status 2 and objective 1 status 1 with timer_remaining_ms=600000. This verifies the current reconstruction, not original final-live pickup behavior.
negative_control: Earlier left strafe from the same post-dialogue checkpoint stopped near (-98.75,85.77,70.07); a click sent no RequestUseObject and objective 3 stayed active (docs/evidence/bootcamp-s5-corpse-approach-20260924.json runs 67-68). Later identical fixed-duration movement replays diverged, one overshooting without use (docs/evidence/bootcamp-s5-single-session-timer-route-20260924.json observation 4). Use visual prompt/position feedback instead of assuming a timing macro is deterministic.
decision: Use the east-side reached viewpoint and actual use prompt as the bounded next client checkpoint. Do not change corpse placement, interaction radius or LOS based on these emulator-only runs; final-live class, geometry, range and trigger remain evidence gaps.
